value.first: Day 1-2: pick a couple of days at home and let her go bare-bottomed from the waist down, no diaper or training pants. Put the potty in the room she plays in and offer a sit every 45-60 minutes, plus first thing after waking and after meals. Keep each sit short, a minute or two, and read a book together so it feels easy. Expect accidents, lots of them, and treat each one calmly as just laundry.
value.second: Day 3-5: you'll start seeing her recognize the urge, maybe pausing or grabbing herself. Name it out loud and walk her to the potty. Stretch the reminders to every couple of hours and let her pull her own pants down so she owns it. A little cheer or sticker for a success goes a long way at this age. Diapers stay for naps and nights for now, that part comes much later.
value.third: Week 2: by now most days should have more catches than misses, and she may start telling you before she goes. Keep the potty accessible and stay matter-of-fact about slip-ups, since stress and pushing tend to backfire. If after two or three weeks she's still resisting hard or holding her stool, that's a sign to pause and try again in a month rather than force it, and worth raising with your doctor if the holding continues.
